title: Senior's toolkit: running tests from the terminal
summary: Create an xUnit v3 project, run it with dotnet test on the Microsoft Testing Platform, pick tests by class, method or trait, and stop CI from passing with zero tests.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: running tests
steps.body: xUnit v3 test projects are small console programs (you can run one with `dotnet run`). With the .NET 10 SDK, `dotnet test` runs them on the **Microsoft Testing Platform** (MTP), switched on once per repository in `global.json`. These are the commands people type every day.

toolkit.what: Create an xUnit v3 test project (templates from the xunit.v3.templates package). Then reference the project under test.
flags: install the templates once per machine
let the tests see the code
toolkit.example:
dotnet new install xunit.v3.templates
dotnet new xunit3 -n Shop.Tests
dotnet add Shop.Tests reference Shop
dotnet sln add Shop.Tests

toolkit.what: global.json at the repository root: makes `dotnet test` use MTP mode (.NET 10 SDK). xUnit v3 4.x runs on MTP v2, which the old VSTest mode no longer runs on the .NET 10 SDK.
flags: .NET 11: an environment variable that overrides global.json

toolkit.what: Build and run the tests. In MTP mode a project or solution is named with --project / --solution.
flags: only these classes (wildcards at either end)

toolkit.what: Fail the run if fewer tests ran. Catches the silent disaster: a filter or a rename that makes CI pass with zero tests.
flags: the run fails below this count
print the tests that would run, run nothing

toolkit.what: Run the test program directly: fastest inner loop, no test host in between.
flags: everything after it goes to the test program
xUnit: stop at the first failing test
print ITestOutputHelper output as tests run

steps.prompt: Match each option to what it does.
pairs: run only the classes whose names end in InvoiceTests
fail the run when fewer than 900 tests ran
show which tests would run without running them
say which test project to build and run

steps.prompt: Someone renamed the test project's folder. CI still shows a green build, but its log says `Total: 0`. Which change makes CI fail loudly next time?
options: Pass `--minimum-expected-tests` with the suite's size (a little below it)
steps.explain: Zero tests is a pass by default: nothing failed. A minimum count turns "we accidentally run nothing" into a red build. Set it a bit below the real count so adding or removing a test does not break CI.

steps.prompt: Run only the shipping tests of `Shop.Tests` and stop at the first failure, by running the test program directly.
steps.explain: An xUnit v3 test project is a program: `dotnet run` builds and starts it, and the arguments after `--` go to the program itself, so its own xUnit options work.

steps.prompt: After upgrading to xUnit v3 4.x on the .NET 10 SDK, `dotnet test` stops with a message that VSTest is not supported for this project. What is the usual fix?
options: Add `"test": { "runner": "Microsoft.Testing.Platform" }` to global.json, so dotnet test runs in MTP mode
Rename the tests to end in `Test`
steps.explain: xUnit v3 4.x targets MTP v2, and the old VSTest bridge does not run MTP v2 projects on the .NET 10 SDK. MTP mode is the current way; VSTest-only options such as `--logger` then no longer apply (MTP has `--report-xunit-trx` and friends).
